hypothesis:
(from Phases 2H.7-2I.1): ranking a target's eligible tracks by
confidence selects that mood's feature-space extreme. Single-target lists are
therefore narrow; two-target uplift lists look diverse largely because they
join two moods' extremes (between-target separation), not because of variety
within each mood. Pools that move picks toward each mood's centre (2I) widen
single-target lists but shrink that separation. H1: choosing the most confident
tracks *within fixed feature cells spanning each target's whole eligible
population* raises within-target diversity in both families without an
uplift regression, while keeping label consistency and classifier agreement.

preregistration.families: Unique effective configurations by (target, share): single-target family = 6 (happy, sad, angry, calm, energetic, stressed; chill/match and stressed/uplift are the same calm:30 and count once); multi-target family = 5 two-target uplift mixes. Families are scored separately.
preregistration.reference: Paired comparisons use G (production + calm guard) as the reference. G is identical to production on every configuration without calm (same seeds, same lists); on calm configurations it removes speech-like tracks, whose feature spread Phase 2H.8.1 established is not a quality gain. Unguarded production is reported alongside.
preregistration.primary_and_secondary: S is the primary candidate. SM is reported as a scoped secondary design and is the proposal candidate only if S fails a multi-target gate while SM passes every gate.
preregistration.diversity_decomposition: list diversity = mean pairwise distance over the whole list (as in all earlier phases); within-target diversity = mean pairwise distance among slots of the same target (pairs pooled); between-target separation = mean distance between slots of different targets (multi-target only).
preregistration.relevance: Measured: label/rule consistency and exact shares (circular by construction). Proxy: classifier agreement (classifier argmax == dataset label) and mean classifier probability on base-label slots. The earlier mean-probability >= 0.99 gate is reported as a legacy reference, not as a gate: Phase 2I showed it confines selection to the confident core, where feature concentration is intrinsic, so with any diversity gate it decides the outcome in advance.
preregistration.seeds: No parameter is tuned: S's 30 cells and CELL_TOP=20 are fixed from the list size and production's 20-per-slot pool. Gates are applied on the primary seeds 24000-24049; replication seeds 27000-27049 are reported and must not reverse a gate decision.
preregistration.uncertainty: Paired per-seed differences against the reference, 2,000-sample percentile bootstrap over the 50 runs; family means bootstrap the per-run mean over the family's configurations. Intervals describe sampling variability on one catalog, not listener-level significance.

gates.integrity: 100% target consistency, exact shares in every list, same-seed determinism on all 12 requests

measured_facts: Which tracks are served, their dataset label / derived-rule membership, exact target shares, repeat rate, unique-track coverage, determinism and latency in this harness.
Audio-feature values (Spotify-derived) and the classifier's probabilities for served tracks.
proxies: Feature-space diversity (mean pairwise distance in 9 z-scored audio features) is a proxy for variety; it is not listener-perceived variety and is inflated by outliers such as speech-like tracks.

Classifier probability and agreement are proxies for mood relevance; the classifier was trained on the same model-generated labels and the ranking optimises its probability, so they are not independent.
Target consistency is circular: candidates are filtered by the same label/rule that defines relevance.
Typicality (distance to the target's eligible centroid) describes where in the mood's feature distribution picks come from; whether central or extreme tracks are 'better' is not measured.
assumptions: The Moodify labels (model-generated, CC BY 4.0) are an acceptable definition of each base mood.
Angry and stressed percentile rules define those moods (stressed is experimental).
More within-mood variety at constant relevance is desirable; no user data confirms this.
measurement_validity.not_measured: No human relevance judgments, listening data, skips, likes or A/B outcomes exist for this catalog; nothing here measures listener satisfaction.

notes: Diversity is feature-space diversity, not listener-perceived variety.
Bootstrap intervals describe sampling variability over 50 seeded runs on one catalog only.
Latency is machine-dependent; variants ran sequentially in one process. S's cells are built once per catalog (cell_build_ms in cold start), not per request.
